plan.vision: A strict Spec Roadmap detailing the exact Agentic problem, atomic milestones, and Testing Strategy. The project aims to create a local, interactive, and self-contained learning environment for developers to learn new programming concepts and languages using an LLM-driven tutor. The tutor will provide interactive lessons, code examples, and exercises, all while running on the user's local machine. Atomic milestones include: 1) Setting up the LLM and core logic, 2) Creating the interactive lesson system, 3) Implementing the exercise and feedback loop, 4) Finalizing the testing and documentation. The Testing Strategy will involve unit tests for the core logic and integration tests for the interactive components.

plan.lessons_learned: This project avoids past mistakes by using memory-mapped files for efficient data handling, prioritizing algorithmic efficiency over OOP overhead, and ensuring that all dependencies are pinned in a virtual environment. The repository will be kept lightweight by excluding heavy directories with .gitignore, and clear setup scripts will be provided for reproducibility. There are no hidden paid-API dependencies.
plan.commit_message: Implement a local, interactive, and self-contained LLM-driven coding tutor.

files_to_generate.instructions: Contains the core logic for loading lessons, processing user input, and generating feedback. Use dependency injection for LLM and other external dependencies.
Handles the management of lessons, including fetching the next lesson and saving progress. Use a simple file-based storage for persistence.
Executes user code and checks if it matches the expected output. Ensure this is done in a safe and isolated environment.
Contains the unit and integration tests for the core logic, lesson manager, and exercise runner. Import and use the actual generated modules without creating mock or stub classes for the core logic.
Exclude venv, __pycache__, .env, and any other heavy directories to keep the repository lightweight.
Provide a detailed explanation of the architecture, setup instructions, and how to run the tests. Include a Mermaid diagram for clarity.
